- Installing a newer APK over the old one keeps the data only when the package name and the signing certificate are identical (Android signing documentation).

- Android's built-in Google Drive backup would copy the database and photos (up to 25 MB) to the user's Google account. It is switched off, because the Functional Analysis says nothing leaves the device.

- Photos are saved in the app's private folder. The pick and shrink steps first write into a temporary cache folder that Android may clear, so the pipeline copies the final file to the permanent folder before saving the card.
- Google's developer verification (2026) may affect installs on other people's phones: a check before sharing, see section 9.3 of the document.
